tagline: Up the Owens Valley to where Los Angeles takes its water.
intro: North of Independence, US 395 runs up the Owens Valley past the small Fort Independence Indian Reservation, through rangeland of big sagebrush and rabbitbrush, toward Big Pine. Near Tinemaha Reservoir the Los Angeles Aqueduct draws its water from the Owens River, and north of that point there is more green to be seen.
Frémont named the valley in 1845 for Richard Owens, one of his guides. Camp Independence was set up on Oak Creek on the Fourth of July, 1862, during the Owens Valley Indian War.

moments.title: Mount Whitney Fish Hatchery
moments.text: A Tudor Revival hatchery on Oak Creek, its walls built of 3,500 tons of granite gathered within a quarter mile, begun in 1916 to match the mountains and last forever.

moments.title: Tinemaha Reservoir
moments.text: A dam on the Owens River holds this link in the Los Angeles Aqueduct, where Roy Rogers filmed Under Western Stars in 1938 and tundra swans come for the winter.
